Byline: Chris Graham and Tom Bennett, reporting from Jerusalem. NOTE: Britain moved to GMT (UTC+0) at 02:00 today, so the trailing Z equals local time exactly.

HEADLINE: Israel to close West Bank crossings on election day as crackdown escalates

CORE FACTS
- All West Bank land crossings will be closed during Tuesday's election in Israel, the country's military says, and Palestinian workers will be barred from entering all settlements.
- IDF announced a "ban on the entry and exit of Palestinian workers throughout Judea and Samaria and the Jordan Valley, including industrial zones, as well as the closure of all land crossings" on Tuesday.
- Most workers would also be barred from settlements from Sunday (today), with the exception of industrial zones and a limited number of other areas.
- Before the 7 October 2023 Hamas-led attack, more than 100,000 Palestinian workers were permitted to enter Israel. Since then only a small fraction have had their permits restored.
- Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said about 2,000 residents had been displaced by the operation.
- At least one whole street appears to have been flattened, according to footage shared online.
- Even before the entry/exit bans were announced by the IDF on Sunday, the military had cordoned off Hebron, heavily restricting the movement of its 200,000 residents.
- Netanyahu announced the operation on Friday after two Israeli soldiers were killed by two Palestinian gunmen at a checkpoint. Three other Israeli soldiers were injured; the gunmen were also killed.
- BBC notes it is common for Israeli forces to demolish homes of Palestinians suspected of attacks, a practice Israeli rights groups have criticised as collective punishment.

NAMED QUOTES
- Hebron Mayor Youssef al-Jaabari said the operation was being "driven by the elections" and that Netanyahu and his ministers were attempting to secure the votes of the far right and the settlers.
- In an interview with Israel's i24 television channel released on Saturday, Netanyahu threatened a "very big surprise" for the Palestinian Authority.
- The October Council (founded by families of victims and hostages of 7 October 2023) wrote on X ahead of Saturday's Tel Aviv rally: "Three days before the election, we will hold the culminating event marking three years of struggle to uncover the truth, demand accountability, and establish a state commission of inquiry."

OTHER
- On Saturday thousands gathered in Tel Aviv for a large anti-government demonstration organised by the October Council. Leaders of the four main opposition parties attended, including Gadi Eisenkot, former military chief of staff, described by the BBC as "neck and neck with Netanyahu".

ABSENCE NOTED: this article makes NO mention of the narrow Friday court order on the Hebron demolitions. Its fate remains unresolved in this source.
